keyed by the variable names of the configured field mapping, the same
mapping a real ingest uses. `kind` is the catalogue the add-in saved
from, or null to read it from `variables` as a "by datacard" watched
folder would. `file_path` is the document's full local path (for
example "C:\DEMO-VAULT\Engineering\Glados\CAD-1001.sldprt"). It is
optional, but only with it can the file be matched to a PDM file and
get the same file-identity checks the API-key surface runs.
PdmValidatePayloadRequest.title: PdmValidatePayloadRequest

PdmValidationResponse.description:

exactly when `reasons` is not empty. `file_identity` is "resolved" or
"unresolved" on the PAT surface, depending on whether `file_path`
matched a known PDM file, and "not_applicable" on the API-key surface,
which already sends a file id. `notes` is advisory context and
`pending_pdm` names the PDM-owned required fields still missing
(typically `part_number` and `revision` before a release); neither
affects `ok`, since the release workflow assigns those fields.
PdmValidationResponse.title: PdmValidationResponse

what the demand needs. MATERIAL_SHORT: a live lot's raw material is
partly unallocated or waits on a line without a delivery date, so its
first step cannot be planned in full. LATE: a live lot is past its

outcome: a `progress` frame before each object is copied (`current`,
`total`, `key`), then exactly one `result` frame (the plain endpoint's
response body) or `error` frame. Requires write:settings.

The copy runs in its own task with its own session, because FastAPI
closes this request's session before the stream sends its first byte. A
client disconnect only ends the stream: the task keeps copying and still
switches the settings once every object is copied, or leaves them as
they were. A server shutdown cancels the task before that final commit,
which leaves the settings unchanged too; copied objects are overwritten
on the next attempt.

for it as moved. All items are booked in one transaction, so an item
that fails leaves every item of the order undelivered. A rejection for

still gets its full remaining quantity delivered. A rejection works as

`body.delivery_note_number` and `body.damage_noted_on_delivery_note`

post.description:
Cancels the lot's raw material demand: records the cancel, releases
every allocation it holds and unlinks it from its lot, so the lot can
demand its material again. Needs the lot's update permission; a
fulfilled or canceled demand answers 409, and so does the demand of a
lot that has started production.

While the lot has not ended, `cancel_lot` is required (422 without it):
true cancels the lot as well, which needs the lot's cancel permission
and settles the demand with it; false cancels only the demand, and the
lot waits on raw material until its source is switched.

put.description:
Sets one of the two statuses a demand takes by hand: `canceled`,
which cancels it as POST /{demand_id}/cancel does, or `fulfilled`, which
marks it fulfilled. Open, allocated and ordered follow from the demand's
allocations and are refused with 422. Needs write:demand_items, and
manage:demand_items for both values, since both are irreversible,
instead of the lot permission the cancel route asks for. Requesting the
status the demand already has returns it unchanged; canceling a
fulfilled demand or marking a canceled one fulfilled answers 409.
`cancel_lot` is the choice the cancel route takes for the lot.
